extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners before the USPTO, Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24 (public reprimand based on another jurisdiction's disciplinary order), including service, response timeline, publication, and notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may request that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by another jurisdiction (e.g., a state supreme court public reprimand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document cites that the request for public reprimand was based on a July 26, 2010 order of the Supreme Court of Florida; action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity to contest (40-day response requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent seeks to contest imposition of the identical discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d), respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response must contain 'all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by [the other jurisdiction] would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for defeating reciprocal discipline — genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid imposition of identical discipline, respondent must raise a genuine issue of material fact under the grounds listed in 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no genuine issue of material fact is shown (or respondent fails to respond), the Director may determine there is no genuine issue and that reciprocal discipline (e.g., public reprimand) is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and mailing standards for Notice and Order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order shall be mailed first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to an address where the OED Director reasonably believes the respondent receives mail (e.g., address listed by the state bar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracking information from USPS showing delivery is used as evidence of service; the Notice and Order in this case was delivered Sept 19, 2011. Proper service and proof of delivery are prerequisites to proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a timely response contesting the discipline, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and impose the identical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order notes Respondent did not file a response and therefore a public reprimand was determined appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and shall publish a notice of reprimand in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must include identifying information and the basis for discipline; the Final Order further indicates disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room (URL provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to state disciplinary agencies and courts (§11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director, in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit post-discipline notice obligation to relevant agencies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for USPTO discipline under 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6) (e.g., being publicly reprimanded by another jurisdiction) can serve as a basis for USPTO public reprimand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Reprimand states Mr. Hurst 'has been publicly reprimanded by the USPTO for violating 37 C.F.R. §10.23(b)(6) by having been publicly reprimanded by the Supreme Court of Florida.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of underlying discipline (example of underlying misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: The underlying state-court discipline (Florida) was predicated on a determination that the practitioner misrepresented his pro bono status while expecting payment, admitting violation of R. Regulating Fla. Bar 4-8.4(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This entry shows the type of misconduct the state court found and which supported the state public reprimand that triggered USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notice should state practitioner's USPTO authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Public reprimand notices should identify the practitioner's licensure and whether the practitioner is a registered patent practitioner authorized to practice patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Notice in this case explicitly states Mr. Hurst is 'authorized to represent others before the USPTO in trademark and non-patent matters' and that 'Mr. Hurst is not a registered patent practitioner and is not authorized to practice patent law before the USPTO.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service details
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of service documenting mailing of the Final Order must identify the date, mailing method (first-class certified mail, return receipt requested), recipient address used (e.g., address listed by state bar), and include signature/date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service that certifies mailing to the address the OED Director reasonably believes the respondent receives mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders specify the statutory and regulatory authority under which the discipline is imposed (e.g., 35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §11.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing the enabling statutes and regulations provides the legal basis and transparency for the disciplinary action and its publication.
